10.2.3 How can I solve it?
MULTIPLE METHODS FOR SOLVING EQUATIONS

Launch
Three friends are trying to work out how many people were in the designated prize-winning seats at a concert. The venue says there were 15 sections with (x + 20) people in each, totaling 525 people. (Let x be the number of prize-winning seats in a section.) They record 15(x + 20) = 525. Then the friends each take a slightly different approach:
FRIEND A: 15(x + 20) = 525; 15x + 300 = 525
FRIEND B: 15(x + 20) = 525; 15(x + 20)/15 = 525/15
FRIEND C: Each section had 35 people, so x + 20 = 35.
Discuss each approach with your team.

Explore
You have solved linear, quadratic, and exponential equations in this course. Sometimes, when an equation looks very complicated, you can rewrite it to make the solving process easier. What are some other ways to solve complicated equations, like (sqrt(x + 5) - 6)^2 + 4 = 20? In this lesson, you will work with your team as you explore additional methods of solving complicated equations.
